sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Antibody-feeding internalization assay (PMC6899438): HA-NL2 is surface-accessible and internalizes to Rab5+ early endosomes and Rab11+ recycling endosomes, confirming surface display. Immunostaining in neurons (PMC11811269): HA-Nlgn2-WT localizes to gephyrin-positive synapses. No neurexin-binding or synapse-formation functional assay reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: All six ledger clips (L1-L6) converge on a single construct: full-length NL2 with an HA tag at its extracellular N-terminus. No residue number is stated in any clip, but the topology is unambiguous: the signal peptide occupies residues 1-14 (MWLLALCLVGLAGA), the mature N-terminus begins at residue 15 (Q), and the C-terminus is intracellular (699-835). Therefore exactly one extracellular terminus exists, and the tag must sit after residue 14 (A) and before residue 15 (Q). Python verification confirms seq[14]='A' and seq[15]='Q'. The site is >=3 residues from the TM boundary (TM starts at 678) and is the canonical position for N-terminal epitope tags on type-I single-pass receptors. Full-length NL2 with HA tag at the extracellular N-terminus expressed in COS-7 cells, HeLa cells, and hippocampal neurons (PMC6899438); and in neurons via lentiviral FSW-hSyn-HA-Nlgn2-WT vector (PMC11811269). No residue number is named in any clip; the junction is derived from the topology: signal peptide spans 1-14, mature N-terminus is residue 15 (Q), and the C-terminus is intracellular, leaving exactly one extracellular terminus at which the tag can sit.

sources.claim: To investigate trafficking of NL2, we used antibody feeding to follow the internalization of NL2 containing an HA tag at its extracellular N terminus ( HA NL2).

literature_notes: All six ledger lines (L1-L6) describe the same construct and the same junction: HA tag at the extracellular N-terminus of full-length NL2, after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 14. L1-L4 come from PMC6899438 (antibody-feeding study); L5-L6 come from PMC11811269 (lentiviral neuronal expression study). Both papers corroborate the same site; L1 is used as the primary supporting clip because it is the most explicit statement of the tag position. No internal loop insertions, C-terminal tags, transposon screens, or FP-fusion data appear in the ledger, so no additional sites are proposed. The C-terminus (699-835) is intracellular and does not qualify as a surface tag site.
